subject: Evidence scope decision: short-window BYOK ask & SSO traceability
messages:
From: Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@stratoshealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: security@stratoshealth.com
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short retention window & BYOK need for Stratos POC

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two quick asks from our side before the POC kickoff:

- We need a 7-day retention window for user-level logs and a way to produce an audit evidence package on demand.
- Because we handle PHI, Stratos needs the option to bring their own keys (BYOK) for model request payload encryption and an auditable key handoff.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: produce an evidence bundle (logs + auth traces) for a date range, and accept a short-lived BYOK model where the key lives in Stratos KMS? If not, what alternatives (ephemeral escrow, HSM integration) are viable?

Attached: high-level requirements doc.

Appreciate a quick triage so procurement can line up the contract items.

Best,
Luis
VP Security, Stratos Health

Attachment: stratos_byo_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@stratoshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Short retention window & BYOK need for Stratos POC

Team — forwarding Stratos' ask to triage. High level points we need to clarify and decide: 

1) Audit evidence: they want on-demand evidence bundles (7-day window initially). Need to confirm format (raw logs vs curated package), required fields (tokens, request/response hashes, SSO identity mapping).
2) BYOK model payload encryption: they want to keep keys in their KMS and have Redwood accept encrypted payloads or hand off keys for decryption.
3) SSO traceability: correlate token/session to SSO identity for audit.
4) Timeline: procurement wants POC in two weeks. Feasible?

Initial asks from me: Jonas, can security outline constraints for accepting external key material or supporting a transient BYOK flow? Marissa, what's the product surface needed to support on-demand evidence bundles and short retention windows without impacting our SLOs? Naomi, any compliance gating for a 7-day retention/ephemeral-key model? Ben, ops: what infra work (logging pipeline, storage isolation, fast export) is required?

I attached their requirements doc. I'll keep Luis on the loop but please reply with a clear set of blockers + recommended path (preferably with a one-paragraph executive summary we can share with procurement).

Thanks — Karthik
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: stratos_byo_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@stratoshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jul 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Short retention window & BYOK need for Stratos POC

Thanks for the clear summary, Karthik. Quick product read:

- Evidence bundle: we can produce a curated export that includes request metadata (timestamp, model ID, route, token usage) and auth traces (SSO ID, session ID) — format would be a gzipped JSON + CSV index. Exporting on-demand is supported by our export job; need to add a small filter for a strict 7-day window. Effort: ~3 engineer-days and 2 infra-days to ensure SLO-safe export.
- Short retention: we already support configurable per-tenant retention, but UI for 7-day override + policy coding is required. Effort: ~3 sprints if prioritized, but we can do a POC flag for this customer in 2 weeks if we accept manual ops steps.
- BYOK: full BYOK for request payload decryption currently isn't productized. Options: (A) temporary escrow where Stratos provides keys for the POC and we rotate immediately after — lower engineering lift, but legal + security sign-off needed; (B) edge-HSM integration — long lead (quarters); (C) accept encrypted payloads and perform validation without decryption (limited usefulness).

Recommended path for POC: do the evidence export + 7-day retention as a gated ops play (manual flag + CLI run). For BYOK, propose temporary escrow flow for POC while we scope a longer-term HSM/KMS integration. We can ship a canary-level CLI + runbook in 2 weeks provided security signs off.

I'll open a GH ticket with acceptance criteria and link.

Marissa
Director, Product Management — Observability, Redwood Inference

Related: GH #prod/exports-546 (https://github.com/redwood/prod/issues/546)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@stratoshealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Short retention window & BYOK need for Stratos POC

Appreciate the clear options, Marissa. Security notes and constraints: 

- Temporary escrow: acceptable for a short POC if keys are rotated immediately after the POC and Stratos signs the MOU. We'll need a documented key custody process and HSM-backed storage on our side for the escrowed key during the window. Controls: least-privilege access, audit logging of key access, and an automated rotation script.
- Direct BYOK (keys never leave Stratos KMS): preferred from a security posture perspective. To enable, we need a decryption proxy pattern where Redwood requests a short-lived decryption token from Stratos KMS at call time OR we implement a client-side encryption handshake. Both require coordination with Stratos' KMS (API access) and will add multi-week integration work.
- Audit evidence: we must include key-access logs (who, when, by which process) in the bundle. If we use escrow, capture HSM access events and rotation records.

Blocking questions:
- Can Stratos provide an API for tokenized decryption (preferred) or is escrow their only option?
- Legal: who signs the key custody MOU? Procurement or Legal?

I'll outline the minimal security checklist for the POC and a set of gating controls we need before starting (I'll attach it to the GH ticket).

-Jonas
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements Team <procurements@stratoshealth.com>, Luis Mendoza <luis.mendoza@stratoshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Short retention window & BYOK need for Stratos POC

Forwarding final triage checklist to procurement and Luis so we can lock timelines. TL;DR: POC approved under temporary escrow + evidence export with strict controls. Items and owners: 

- Legal/Procurement (Procurements Team): sign a short Key Custody MOU and add an exhibit for rotation and deletion. (Owner: Procurements Team)
- Security (Jonas): provide HSM-backed escrow procedures, rotation automation, and on-demand key-access audit export. (Owner: Jonas Weber)
- Product (Marissa): implement the export filter for 7-day window and provide a runbook for manual POC operations. (Owner: Marissa Cole)
- Ops (Ben): stand up an isolated export job runner with access controls and verify SLO impact. (Owner: Ben Carter)
- Sales Eng (Karthik): coordinate kickoff, acceptance criteria, and 2-week timeline check-ins. (Owner: Karthik Iyer)

Procurement: please review the attached redlined MSA + exhibit and confirm whether Stratos can sign within five business days. If yes, we'll schedule the POC kickoff for Mon, Jul 24. If there are additional regulatory controls required, flag them now.
